summary: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

A security regression (CVE-2006-5051) was discovered in OpenSSH's server (sshd). There is a race condition which can lead sshd to handle some signals in an unsafe manner. An unauthenticated, remote attacker may be able to trigger it by failing to authenticate within a set time period.

SGLang allows unauthenticated pickle deserialization through /update_weights_from_tensor when no auth keys are configured, and the SafeUnpickler policy can be bypassed because builtins.import and builtins.getattr are resolvable, enabling code execution via pickle REDUCE.

Komodo through 2.3.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Periphery agent that allows unauthenticated attackers to connect as a trusted Core because empty core_public_keys and passkeys lists fail open by default. Attackers reaching port 8120 can present any generated keypair to issue Periphery API requests, including terminal sessions and container operations, executing commands on managed hosts typically as root.

Description:

When an iRule that processes client traffic using the GENERICMESSAGE::route command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). 





Impact:



Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.







Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A flaw was found in the libreswan client plugin for NetworkManager (NetkworkManager-libreswan), where it fails to properly sanitize the VPN configuration from the local unprivileged user. In this configuration, composed by a key-value format, the plugin fails to escape special characters, leading the application to interpret values as keys. One of the most critical parameters that could be abused by a malicious user is the `leftupdown`key. This key takes an executable command as a value and is used to specify what executes as a callback in NetworkManager-libreswan to retrieve configuration settings back to NetworkManager. As NetworkManager uses Polkit to allow an unprivileged user to control the system's network configuration, a malicious actor could achieve local privilege escalation and potential code execution as root in the targeted machine by creating a malicious configuration.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.13, FortiOS 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or command via crafted packets.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken access control and path traversal vulnerability in the fax/sms module disposeDocument action via an unvalidated file_path parameter. Authenticated low-privilege users can read sqlconf.php to recover database credentials and write arbitrary files as the web user, enabling remote code execution.

Cockpit's remote login feature passes user-supplied hostnames and usernames from the web interface to the SSH client without validation or sanitization. An attacker with network access to the Cockpit web service can craft a single HTTP request to the login endpoint that injects malicious SSH options or shell commands, achieving code execution on the Cockpit host without valid credentials. The injection occurs during the authentication flow before any credential verification takes place, meaning no login is required to exploit the vulnerability.

A flaw was found in Jolokia's JSR-160 proxy functionality where insufficient validation of client-controlled JMX service URLs allows a bypass of the denylist introduced to mitigate CVE-2018-1000130. The proxy accepts a `target.url` value from a Jolokia POST request and passes it to `JMXServiceURL` and `JMXConnectorFactory` for establishing the remote JMX connection. The existing denylist only rejects URLs matching `service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/ldap:.*`, which can be bypassed using alternative valid JMX service URL forms, including `ldaps://` schemes or LDAP URLs with a non-empty JMX host component. These URLs are accepted as valid `JMXServiceURL` objects and can cause the Jolokia agent JVM to perform a JNDI lookup against an attacker-controlled LDAP endpoint. This can result in server-side request forgery (SSRF), forwarding of supplied JMX credentials to the remote endpoint, and potentially remote code execution depending on the classes and configuration available in the target JVM.

A remote code execution vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. Insufficient bounds validation in the AV1 encoder's SVC (Scalable Video Coding) layer ID control allows an attacker to supply crafted video frame pixels that overlap with internal encoder layer context structures. In fork-based video processing services, an attacker can use this to hijack the cyclic refresh map pointer, brute-force the process base address via a crash oracle, and redirect control flow to achieve arbitrary command execution. Exploitation requires the target service to use libaom with SVC encoding enabled and accept attacker-supplied video frames.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains a stack-based buffer overflow in the NAS TFTP service that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service or potential code execution.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service or potential code execution on the NAS node.

Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the earlier CVE-2026-67429 remediation applied validate_path_with_env_config() to only a hand-picked set of file-writing modules, leaving data.csv.write in src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py, data.json_to_csv in src/core/modules/atomic/data/json_to_csv.py, file.copy in src/core/modules/atomic/file/copy.py, and file.move in src/core/modules/atomic/file/move.py outside the FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR confinement boundary. The advisory also identifies unguarded modules across the broader data.*, file.*, and report-writer families. data.csv.write relies on a .. substring denylist that does not reject absolute paths, while the other named modules accept caller-controlled output or destination paths without the canonical guard. A caller able to execute modules or recipes can therefore write attacker-controlled content outside the configured sandbox, potentially overwriting application code, recipes, startup files, scheduled-task files, or authorization files and gaining code execution on the host. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

Joomla Extension - valorapps.com - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Easy File Uploader < 2.9.7 - An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload a PHP-executable file to the Joomla web root with a single multipart POST request, requiring no credentials and no CSRF token.

Description: 
BIG-IP iControl REST tokens may not expire as expected in all scenarios.   

Impact: 
An attacker who has obtained a token may be able to extend its expiry lifetime unless the token owner deletes it. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A race condition vulnerability was discovered in how signals are handled by OpenSSH's server (sshd). If a remote attacker does not authenticate within a set time period, then sshd's SIGALRM handler is called asynchronously. However, this signal handler calls various functions that are not async-signal-safe, for example, syslog(). As a consequence of a successful attack, in the worst case scenario, an attacker may be able to perform a remote code execution (RCE) as an unprivileged user running the sshd server.

Previously, CVE-2024-45337 fixed an authorization bypass for misused ssh server configurations; if any other type of callback is passed other than public key, then the source-address validation would be skipped.

Confused deputy in Sync in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via crafted network traffic. (Chromium security severity: High)

Use after free in WebView in Google Chrome on on Android prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via crafted network traffic. (Chromium security severity: Critical)

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to authenticate as any trusted certificate by appending its public certificate to their presented TLS client chain. Attackers can append the server's or a cluster member's certificate to gain cluster-level access, bypass authorization, modify trust store entries, and influence scriptlet-based authorization decisions.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c` in `nvmet_tcp_free_crypto` due to a logical bug in the NVMe/TCP subsystem in the Linux kernel. This issue may allow a malicious user to cause a use-after-free and double-free problem, which may permit remote code execution or lead to local privilege escalation.

A flaw was found in CRIU's handling of restartable sequences (rseq) during checkpoint/restore. A malicious process inside a container can register an rseq critical section that hijacks CRIU's parasite code injection during checkpoint, allowing it to spoof the process credentials saved in the checkpoint image. On restore, the container process gains elevated capabilities and zeroed UIDs/GIDs.

The practical impact on Red Hat products is limited by several factors: checkpoint/restore requires root privileges (podman) or cluster-admin RBAC (OpenShift) to trigger and cannot be initiated from within the container itself; on OpenShift prior to 4.17 the feature required explicit opt-in, and on 4.17+ the kubelet checkpoint API RBAC is not configured by default; OpenShift enforces user namespaces by default for regular workloads (hostUsers is gated behind admin-only SCCs), which makes the spoofed capabilities namespace-scoped and ineffective for privilege escalation; SELinux type enforcement (container_t) blocks privilege transitions independently of capabilities; seccomp filters persist through checkpoint/restore and cannot be corrupted via the parasite; and kernel mount namespace ownership checks on RHEL 9/10 kernels prevent mount-based container escape even with spoofed capabilities.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with `ansible-galaxy collection install`, the archive extractor validates member paths using lexical path normalisation (os.path.abspath) instead of resolving symbolic links (os.path.realpath), and it performs no containment check on symlink-typed directory members before creating them. A crafted collection tarball can chain symlink directory entries so that a subsequent file member is written outside the intended destination directory. This allows an attacker who can get a victim to install a malicious collection to overwrite arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running ansible-galaxy, leading to code execution on the control node. This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2020-10691.

A flaw was found in pappl-retrofit. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied filenames when handling the upload and deletion of PostScript Printer Description (PPD) files. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this directory traversal flaw by submitting filenames containing path traversal sequences. This allows the attacker to upload or delete arbitrary files on the system, which can result in data corruption, denial of service, or arbitrary command execution.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O, where it can be requested to take a checkpoint archive of a container and later be asked to restore it. When it does that restoration, it attempts to restore the mounts from the restore archive instead of the pod request. As a result, the validations run on the pod spec, verifying that the pod has access to the mounts it specifies are not applicable to a restored container. This flaw allows a malicious user to trick CRI-O into restoring a pod that doesn't have access to host mounts. The user needs access to the kubelet or cri-o socket to call the restore endpoint and trigger the restore.

A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A flaw in the AV1 encoder's Look-Ahead Processing (LAP) mode causes the first-pass stats ring buffer wrap-around guard to be bypassed when g_lag_in_frames is set to 1 or higher. This results in a 232-byte out-of-bounds write on every encoded frame after the second, corrupting adjacent heap objects. An attacker who can influence encoder configuration in a transcoding service or WebRTC session could exploit this to cause a denial of service (process crash) or potentially achieve code execution.

SmarterTools SmarterMail Insufficient Entropy Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the generation of Application Passwords. The issue results from using insufficient entropy in the generation of credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-33568.

A flaw was found in gst-plugins-base. A heap buffer overflow can be triggered when processing video buffers whose attached GstVideoMeta metadata declares plane strides and offsets that exceed the actual backing memory allocation. The metadata is not range-checked during deserialization, and the video frame mapping code does not verify that the declared plane geometry fits within the buffer before allowing consumers to read or write video data. A local attacker who controls the sending side of a GStreamer inter-process IPC pipeline can deliver a crafted buffer carrying fabricated strides, causing the receiving process to read or write beyond heap boundaries. Successful exploitation can cause a denial of service or potentially allow code execution within the affected process.

A DLL search order hijacking vulnerability in Thermalright TR-VISION HOME on Windows (64-bit) allows a local attacker to escalate privileges via DLL side-loading. The application loads certain dynamic-link library (DLL) dependencies using the default Windows search order, which includes directories that may be writable by non-privileged users.



Because these directories can be modified by unprivileged users, an attacker can place a malicious DLL with the same name as a legitimate dependency in a directory that is searched before trusted system locations. When the application is executed, which is always with administrative privileges, the malicious DLL is loaded instead of the legitimate library.



The application does not enforce restrictions on DLL loading locations and does not verify the integrity or digital signature of loaded libraries. As a result, attacker-controlled code may be executed within the security context of the application, allowing arbitrary code execution with elevated privileges.



Successful exploitation requires that an attacker place a crafted malicious DLL in a user-writable directory that is included in the application's DLL search path and then cause the affected application to be executed. Once loaded, the malicious DLL runs with the same privileges as the application.



This issue affects 
TR-VISION HOME  versions up to and including 2.0.5.

Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps, which calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types. Attackers can supply crafted PostScript or PDF documents that trigger a type error, recover .forceput via a custom error handler, and cause a use-after-free across save/restore to execute arbitrary code.

A maliciously crafted DLL placed in a predictable, attacker-writable temporary directory used by the Autodesk Installer can lead to privilege escalation to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM due to insufficient validation of loaded libraries. An attacker with local and low-privilege access could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM.

OFFIS DCMTK 3.7.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in togglePlanarConfiguration8 and togglePlanarConfiguration16 in djcodece.cc, which compute row offsets using rows instead of columns. Attackers can supply a crafted color-by-plane DICOM image with more rows than columns that is compressed with the true-lossless JPEG codec to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially code execution.

Cozy Cloud cozy-stack 1.6.62 before 1.6.69 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the shared-drive move handler that allows authenticated users to access other instances' files. Attackers owning a shared drive can name another instance's domain and any directory ID as the move source to copy and delete the victim's file tree.

An arbitrary address write vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A missing bounds check in the SVC (Scalable Video Coding) layer ID control function allows an attacker to inject an arbitrary pointer into the cyclic refresh map field via crafted image pixel values. The encoder then writes approximately 1,200 bytes at the attacker-controlled address. This is fully deterministic and does not require a separate information leak. An attacker who can supply frames to a network-facing libaom encoder with SVC enabled could exploit this for denial of service or potential code execution.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization bypass vulnerability. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to act under another user's session, potentially leading to denial of service.

A flaw was found in libsoup. A malicious HTTP/2 server or a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacker can exploit a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the HTTP/2 client implementation. This occurs when a GNOME application uploads a file using HTTP/2, and the server sends a GOAWAY frame while the file body is being read asynchronously. This can lead to memory corruption, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

A flaw was found in libarchive. On 32-bit systems, an integer overflow vulnerability exists in the zisofs block pointer allocation logic. A remote attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted ISO9660 image, which can lead to a heap buffer overflow. This could potentially allow for arbitrary code execution on the affected system.

In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

Dell PowerProtect Data Domain, Feature Release versions 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 release versions 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 release versions 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 release versions 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20, contain an Improper Authentication vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution with root privileges. This is a critical severity vulnerability as it allows an attacker to take complete control of the system. Dell recommends customers to upgrade at the earliest opportunity.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in the package broker in Devolutions Agent 2026.3.0 and 2026.2.4 on Windows allows a local authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands with elevated privileges via crafted custom package parameters.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability that could allow an attacker with internal network access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the NAS node.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability that could allow an attacker with internal network access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the NAS node.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in QEMU's 9pfs subsystem. A race condition between the main thread and a worker thread when processing concurrent Tlcreate and Twalk requests allows a malicious guest user to craft a fid path containing stale heap data, bypassing directory traversal restrictions and escaping the shared directory boundary. This can lead to arbitrary host file read/write and code execution (VM escape) as the QEMU process user.

A improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2 all versions, FortiManager 8.0.0, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2 all versions may allow an authenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via a crafted HTTP request.

SmarterTools SmarterMail File Edit API Directory Traversal Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the FileStorageController class. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-30742.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 remote code execution was possible via a file write bypass in the Kotlin DSL sandbox

yt-mcp is a YouTrack MCP server for Claude Code. Prior to 1.18.1, add_attachment in src/yt_mcp/tools/attachments.py accepts a caller-controlled file_path, checks only that the file exists, reads it without directory confinement, and uploads the bytes to a YouTrack issue. A compromised MCP client or an LLM steered by indirect prompt injection can read any file accessible to the server process and exfiltrate secrets through an issue the caller can access. The same release also permits get_project_health to interpolate a caller-controlled project value into snapshot filenames, allowing parent-directory traversal to write JSON files outside the snapshots directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.18.1.

A command injection flaw was found in the text editor Emacs. It could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary shell commands on a vulnerable system. Exploitation is possible by tricking users into visiting a specially crafted website or an HTTP URL with a redirect.

A flaw was found in dracut. A remote attacker on the adjacent network can exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted DHCP options, such as a malicious root-path, next-server, or bootfile name, to a system using dracut's NetworkManager-based initrd network module. These options are improperly handled and written into a temporary shell script without proper escaping, leading to command injection. This allows the attacker to achieve root code execution within the initramfs during system boot.

A flaw was found in the ContentRepositoryImpl.copyExplodedContent function of the wildfly-core library, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to manage server deployments. The issue occurs when the library processes an unsanitized deployment name. Due to a missing containment check, an attacker with the Deployer RBAC role can use path traversal sequences to access files outside the restricted deployment directory. This can allow the attacker to delete arbitrary directories or create files with arbitrary content, leading to a full privilege escalation to the management SuperUser role.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the FaxSMS module's RCFaxClient and SignalWireClient disposeDocument functions that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read and overwrite arbitrary files via the unsanitized file_path parameter. Attackers can request action=download to retrieve cleartext files like sqlconf.php database credentials and keys, or use action=setup to overwrite web-server-writable files with ciphertext.

The labeled-response module in UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 before 6.2.7.1 does not escape the IRCv3 "label" message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.

A flaw was found in Cockpit. Deleting a sosreport with a crafted name via the Cockpit web interface can lead to a command injection vulnerability, resulting in privilege escalation. This issue affects Cockpit versions 270 and newer.

A malicious actor with access to the network and low privileges could exploit an Improper Link Resolution Before File Access vulnerability found in UniFi Access Application to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the host device.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the Apps edit, Containers edit, and Playbooks execute permissions could use the App Wizard to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR. This could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the Splunk SOAR instance.
The vulnerability exists because the App Wizard does not validate user-supplied identifiers before incorporating them into generated connector code.

A flaw was found in libvirt. A local attacker, specifically a process running as the confined `swtpm` user, could exploit a symlink-following vulnerability in the `virFileChownFiles()` function. By planting a symbolic link within the `swtpm` state directory, the attacker could trick the root-level libvirt daemon into changing the ownership of an arbitrary file to the `swtpm` user. This allows for privilege escalation from the `swtpm` sandbox to root-level file ownership control.

A vulnerability in CRI-O checkpoint restore allows a user who can create a pod from a malicious checkpointed container to bypass the destination Kubernetes security context. The restored process may retain credentials, Linux capabilities, no_new_privs, and seccomp state from the checkpoint instead of enforcing the destination configuration. This can allow execution with elevated privileges across the container security boundary.
Affected upstream supported versions are CRI-O 1.34 and later. Downstream Red Hat products are affected from OCP 4.17 onward. Fixes have been applied to supported branches but are not yet released.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio

For a fault in a private mapping with nothing in the page cache,
hugetlb_no_page() allocates a folio, locks it and maps it.  The folio has
one reference, which belongs to the page table entry from then on.  After
dropping the page table lock the function still sets the migratable flag
of the folio and unlocks it.

Whoever zaps the entry in between frees the folio.  The fault holds the
fault mutex and the lock of the vma.  MADV_DONTNEED and the first unmap of
a hole punch, hugetlb_vmdelete_list(), do not take the fault mutex, and a
private vma only has a lock if it owns a reservation map: not with
MAP_NORESERVE, and not in the child after fork().

Then the flag is set in, and folio_unlock() is called on, a folio that is
free or has a new owner.  A surplus page goes back to the page allocator
while it is locked:

  BUG: Bad page state in process init  pfn:108e00
  flags: 0x200000000000059(locked|uptodate|dirty|head|node=0|zone=2)
  page dumped because: PAGE_FLAGS_CHECK_AT_FREE flag(s) set

A page of the pool can be given to the next user, of any file, who locks
it and loses the lock to the late folio_unlock():

  kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:1532!
   hugetlb_no_page+0x111b/0x23e0
   hugetlb_fault+0x3a9/0x14a0

An unprivileged process is enough: threads that write to a MAP_PRIVATE |
MAP_NORESERVE hugetlb mapping, threads that call MADV_DONTNEED on it, and
one that takes the freed pages for another file.

Until commit 3a47c54f09c4 ("hugetlbfs: revert use i_mmap_rwsem for more
pmd sharing synchronization") the fault held i_mmap_rwsem for reading,
which everybody who zaps takes for writing.  The lock that commit
bf4916922c60 ("hugetlbfs: extend hugetlb_vma_lock to private VMAs") gave
to private vmas closed the window again, but only for those with a
reservation map.

Be done with the folio before the page table lock is dropped, as
hugetlb_wp() is with its copy.  The function already unlocks page cache
folios under that lock.

Original fix generated by an LLM and sent in private by Josef.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR by installing a malicious app.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict app dependencies to validated binary packages before installing them.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps:edit permission could install a connector app that causes Splunk SOAR to write attacker-controlled files outside the app directory. This could let the user modify files used by Splunk SOAR and execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR constructs the dependency installation command from app-supplied metadata without preventing that metadata from changing its arguments.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

f2fs: bound the SIT/NAT bitmaps by the checkpoint pack

sit_ver_bitmap_bytesize and nat_ver_bitmap_bytesize are used as memcpy
lengths into and out of sbi->ckpt, which is sized from cp_payload alone,
and nothing compares either length against that allocation.

sanity_check_ckpt() has checked these two fields since c77ec61ca0a4, which
added them after a crafted image overran build_sit_info(). That check ties
each length to a segment count; it never compares either against the
allocation, which is the half this adds.

Mounting over-reads in build_sit_info() and build_node_manager(), and the
first checkpoint writes the same lengths back through the same pointers,
so the over-read's contents reach the on-disk checkpoint. An unmount is
enough; the filesystem does not have to be used.

Bound both ends the way __bitmap_ptr() lays them out. The three branches
differ, so a single sum of the two lengths would still admit a small
overflow when cp_payload is non-zero.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit

Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug")
made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting
them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast
cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins
at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file.

truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private
COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to
5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has
written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is
lost: it reads the contents of the file again.

Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the
right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that
it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get
rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake
offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical
addresses of more than 32 bits.

Cast to u64 instead. Nothing changes for 64-bit kernels.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab()

Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call
mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object.
__mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range,
so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails.
Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm
reference was acquired.

Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While
we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes
the code more robust.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast

With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can
write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught
empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check.

Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a
userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before
starting the walk, just like GUP-slow.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs

A PMD migration entry can refer to a device-private folio.
zap_huge_pmd_folio() checks the folio type instead of the entry type,
so it treats such a migration entry as a device-private entry.

Installing the migration entry already removed the reverse mapping and
dropped the mapping reference. Zapping it must not repeat those
operations. Concurrent MADV_DONTNEED during migration back to system
memory can trigger this.

Check the PMD entry type using pmd_is_device_private_entry().

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping

zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling folio_mark_dirty().
If this was the last mapping, truncation can skip unmapping the folio
and proceed without waiting for the PMD lock, racing with dirtying.

ifs_set_range_dirty() can oops if MADV_DONTNEED races with
ftruncate() on XFS, when we get the folio set dirty after it was found
to not be mapped anymore.

Move folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_accessed() before rmap removal,
matching the PTE zap path. This keeps the folio mapped while updating
its state, so truncation must wait for the page table lock.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables

MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and
walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become
stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE
table concurrently.

This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU:
support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent
bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged:
retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent
retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking
for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection.

The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to
speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the
RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD
handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all
cases.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

An issue in the TP-Link MQTT Broker and API gateway of TP-Link Kasa KP125M v1.0.3 and Tapo P125M v1.0.2 allows attackers to establish connections by impersonating devices owned by other users.

The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".
